subject: Computer Networking
title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
description: A micro-lesson that makes Post-Quantum Cryptography usable.

hook.text: Quantum computers will break RSA and ECC. Every secure connection on the internet is at risk.

buildup.text: Shor's algorithm factors large numbers fast on quantum hardware. RSA depends on that being hard.

discovery.text: NIST standardized four post-quantum algorithms in 2024. They resist quantum on classical hardware.

twist.text: 'Harvest now, decrypt later' is real. Adversaries store traffic to crack when quantum arrives.

climax.text: Chrome and Signal ship post-quantum key exchange. Billions of systems still need the upgrade.

punchline.text: Quantum will break today's crypto. The migration can't wait.

quiz.question: What is a 'harvest now, decrypt later' attack?
options: Storing encrypted data now to decrypt it when quantum computers exist
Stealing encryption keys from servers in real time
Using quantum computers to break encryption instantly

details.summary: Post-quantum cryptography develops encryption algorithms that resist attacks from both classical and quantum computers. NIST has standardized lattice-based and hash-based algorithms to replace RSA and elliptic curve cryptography before quantum computers become powerful enough to break them.
details.whyItMatters: Quantum computers will eventually break the public-key encryption protecting all internet traffic. Migrating to post-quantum algorithms now protects against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.
takeaways: Quantum computers will break RSA and elliptic curve encryption
NIST standardized post-quantum algorithms including CRYSTALS-Kyber
Migration must happen before quantum computers become practical

faq.question: What is the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat?
faq.answer: Adversaries can record encrypted traffic today and store it until quantum computers can decrypt it. Sensitive data with long-term value like government secrets, medical records, and intellectual property is already at risk from this strategy.

faq.question: How do post-quantum algorithms work?
faq.answer: Post-quantum algorithms are based on mathematical problems that quantum computers cannot solve efficiently. Lattice-based algorithms use the hardness of shortest-vector problems. Hash-based signatures rely on hash function security. These problems resist both classical and quantum attack methods.
